statement: A failed partition-callback read surfaces as a typed owner outcome, never as a clean empty result: PartitionCallbackDispatcher partitions its per-partition results instead of filtering them (failedPartitions carrying partitionId/error/errorCode/participantNodeId/retryAfterMs/backpressured from the existing buildPartitionExecutionFailureResult fields), returns a non-success outcome when every partition failed, and carries failedPartitions through executePartitionCallback into hostResult so artifacts record '1 partition, 1 failed' instead of totalPartitions 0; callback reads also pass executionOptions (tableName + resolveRoutedDeliveryPriority) so system-table callback reads ride the same critical delivery lane and table attribution as executeSelect; and the examples-catalog scenario's anti-affinity inversion (non-seed-first candidate order discarding the resolved replica host when it is the seed) is corrected so the resolved host is the first candidate, with the zero-partition response becoming a thrown failover trigger for free. Verified at HEAD 5da367c47 across four archived runs (ec-final-20260810T14*): the two failing runs show 7 and 3 in-window ACK timeouts delivering to nodes-p1 replicas on the stalled seed (event-loop gaps 1.1-1.9s, ELU 0.91-0.97) with zero timeouts in the two passing runs; the dispatcher's success-only filter (partition-callback-dispatcher.js:138-145) converts the total failure to success:true/batches:[] (hostResult totalPartitions 0), test-locked at partition-callback-dispatcher.test.js:122; nodes-p1 replicas never left the seed in any run (placement/lag/split sub-faces refuted by snapshots). ARCH-0139: missing rows must surface as typed owner outcomes; the sibling executeSelect path already propagates partition failure correctly. Fail-closed floor: partial success (some partitions failing) stays a typed partial outcome, never all-or-nothing data loss; the ReadIndex named wheel is explicitly out of scope (reads failed on transport, not staleness).
